$comment: Sentence-level evidence map for GitHub issue #37. Sentence text is VERBATIM from the issue body (gh issue view 37 --json body); `sep` is the whitespace that follows the sentence in the original (" " same line, "\n" end of source line). Per-link `strength` follows the test index's own convention: `asserted` when the sentence's fact appears in that test's `asserts` list, `exercised` when the test necessarily goes through it but never asserts it. A sentence with no evidence is deliberately left with tests:[] and strength:null - no colour, no warning, no finding.
$comment2: Each sentence carries one `coverage` value - the colour. It answers 'how much of what this sentence CLAIMS is proven', not 'how many tests touch it'. The per-link `strength` below it is unchanged and still describes one test's relationship to the sentence.
$comment3: Blocks mirror the issue's markdown skeleton: `p`, `hr`, `h2` (a `## ` heading) and `ol` (a numbered list whose items hold the sentences). Reconstruction is `"".join(text + sep)` per paragraph/list item, `"## " + text` per heading, `"N. "` per list item, blank line between blocks - build_mapping.py asserts the result equals `gh issue view 37 --json body` character for character. Sentence text keeps its `**bold**` markers so that stays true, and the renderer turns them into <strong>. The body is deliberately NOT hard-wrapped - one line per paragraph, list item and heading - so `sep` is a plain space almost everywhere and the tab wraps text to its own column instead of to whatever column the author typed in. The renderer still folds a stray newline inside a paragraph to a space, as defence against the issue being re-wrapped later.

issue.title: Link Visit with Vet
issue.author: victorrentea
issue.$facts: author/createdAt come from `gh issue view 37 --json author,createdAt`; the avatar is inlined as a data URI by build_asset.py because the report is opened from file:// and a remote would not load.

legend.$rule: Red and no-colour both mean 'no test'. The difference between them is the whole point of the scale: red is a claim about the software that nothing proves; no colour is a sentence that makes no such claim, so there is nothing to prove. A sentence is coloured for what it CLAIMS, not for how many tests happen to run through it.
legend.covered: full green - every claim it makes is in a test's assertion.
legend.partly: half green - part of what it claims is asserted; another part has no test behind it.
legend.exercised: orange - a test goes through it and never checks it.
legend.missing: full red - a testable claim no test asserts, or even reaches.
legend.none: no colour - not a claim about the software: a heading, the reason behind a rule, a scope exclusion, or a note about the ticket's own history. Nothing to cover, so nothing missing.

$legendNote: Four steps, not five. `exercised` (orange) already IS the 'reached but unproven' step, so a half-red 'partly missing' would name the same state as half-green 'partly covered' from the other end - two shades of different hue for one condition, which is the ambiguity worth avoiding. There is no half-orange either: nothing in this map is partly-walked-through, and a fifth tint between half-green and orange is not one a reader could name.

evidenceStrength.asserted: The fact is in a test's assertion.
evidenceStrength.exercised: A test necessarily goes through it, but never asserts it.
evidenceStrength.touched: Merely reached; no claim made about it.

categories.$derivation: Derived at build time, never hand-listed. First authority is which test-index file the id appears in (browser.json -> e2e, rest.json and mcp.json -> api); a test the index has not picked up yet falls back to path shape: petclinic-test/** is e2e, src/test/java/**/rest/** and src/test/java/**/mcp/** are api, any other src/test/java/** is unit. Add a test and it classifies itself.
categories.$mcp: MCP sits under `api`, not on its own. It is a second machine-facing contract over the same service layer - it answers the same question REST does (does the contract carry the vet) and drives no browser. It also has no linked test on this branch, so a separate group would render as an empty box.
categories.$rendered: Only categories with members are drawn. On this branch that is e2e and api; `unit` classifies but nothing in this map lands there, so no empty group appears.

sentences.text: The Visit should be linked to the vet that attended that consultation.
sentences.gap: No test supplies an unknown or invalid vetId - every one of them books with a vet that already exists on the roster.

tests.why: POST with a vetId returns 201 and the persisted visit's vet is that vet.
PUT with a vetId reassigns the attending vet, verified against the database after flush+clear.
GET /api/visits/{id} returns the linked vet's id, first name and last name.
Browser to API to DB round trip: the vet chosen in the form is the vet on the resulting visit row.
Names a vet from the roster up front, books with her, and reads that same name back off the pet's history - an independent oracle rather than a round trip.

sentences.text: Visit should display its vet everywhere throughout the app.
sentences.gap: The MCP side shows no vet at all and nothing covers it; the visit edit screen is never opened by a browser test.

tests.why: Deep-equal of every rendered row against the API, vet name included.
The vet's name appears on the visit row of the owner detail page.
The vet's name is on the DTO every screen reads from.
The owner page shows the named attending vet on the booked visit.

sentences.text: **Booking a visit lets you choose the vet, and lets you not choose one.**
sentences.gap: One named vet is now proven selectable, but the option list as a whole is still never compared with the roster, and nothing asserts the field is not marked required.

tests.why: Books a visit choosing a vet; that vet's name is on the resulting row.
Books a visit leaving the dropdown alone; the visit appears with an em dash for the vet.
POST with a vetId, 201 Created, vet persisted on the visit.
POST with no vetId, 201 Created, visit persisted.
Chooses a named vet in the form and the history shows her.
Books with nobody attending and the visit is created.

sentences.text: The vet is optional: half the time the appointment is booked before anyone knows who is taking it, and forcing a choice there produces bad data rather than information.
sentences.gap: Optionality is proven at creation only - nothing now shows a visit may be left without a vet later in its life.

tests.why: Submitting the New Visit form without a vet returns to the owner page and the visit appears.
POST /api/visits with no vetId, 201 Created, visit persisted.
A visit booked with nobody attending is created and reads as having no vet.

sentences.text: **Editing a visit can change the vet, and can remove it.**
sentences.gap: “And can remove it” has nothing behind it: no test sends a PUT that omits vetId, and no browser test opens the edit screen.

tests.why: Setting/changing the vet on an existing visit.

sentences.text: Clearing the field must persist as empty.
sentences.gap: Still nothing - the new Gherkin included. “A visit nobody attended” books without a vet, which is a different claim from clearing a vet that was already assigned. Nothing sends a PUT that omits vetId, and no browser test opens the visit edit screen. A structural API diff cannot see it either, since VisitFieldsDto carries an optional vetId under both readings - the behaviour still works, it is simply unproven.

sentences.text: We had this with pet types: the old value kept coming back.
**Wherever a visit is shown with its details, the vet is shown too.**
sentences.gap: The MCP tool list_visits also shows visits with their details, and shows no vet; nothing covers it.

tests.why: Deep-equal of every rendered row against the API, vet name included.
Vet name on the owner page's visit row.
The vet's name is on the DTO every screen reads from.

sentences.text: Today that means the owner's page and the all-visits screen.
sentences.gap: The owner-page check uses toContainText against the whole visit row, not the .visit-vet cell its no-vet sibling scopes to.

tests.why: Owner page, vet present.
Owner page, vet absent.

sentences.gap: It is asserted as an em dash (VetNamePipe.NOT_ATTENDED), a character the ticket never asked for by name.

sentences.text: Not "Unknown", not blank-because-broken, and never an error.

sentences.gap: The test never distinguishes pre-existing rows from the ones it created, and “will not get one” is a non-event no test can prove.

uncolouredRationale.s7: A reference to an older defect in pet types. It is a note about the ticket's own history, not a claim about this system - the behaviour it warns about is the sentence before it, which is red.
uncolouredRationale.s13: A scope exclusion. No test proves the absence of a feature; the owner-search scenarios filter by owner last name, not by vet.
